- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add 1–3% to forecast for momentum bias.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — when price deviates >3σ from 30-day moving average, forecast should be adjusted toward mean with 1–2 day lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in early days of the forecast window; increase initial forecast by 1–2% to account for short-term momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3 in 3–5 days), model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
